title: CAPIT FAQs | Data, Token, and Wallet Answers
description: Answers to common questions about CAPIT's well-plugging data, how tokens are minted, wallets, and what CAPIT does and doesn't claim.
headline: Frequently Asked Questions
body: Clear answers about where CAPIT's data comes from, how records are counted, how the token works, and what CAPIT can and can't do.

sections.heading: What is CAPIT?
sections.body: CAPIT is a public, source-linked registry of U.S. plugged oil and gas well records, paired with a token on the Base network. It organizes records published by state regulators, shows where each one came from, and displays token mint activity next to the underlying data. CAPIT is owned and operated by Tellus Digital, LLC.

sections.heading: Does CAPIT plug wells or pay for plugging?
sections.body: No. Wells are plugged by operators, state agencies, and their contractors. CAPIT tracks the public records of that work. Buying or holding CAPIT does not pay for plugging a well.

sections.heading: How does CAPIT define a plugged well?
sections.body: CAPIT follows the source agency's definition. A well counts when the state regulator's record shows a completed plugging status, such as Plugged & Abandoned. Status terms differ by state, so CAPIT shows the original source term next to its own display label. See [What Is a Plugged Well?](/what-is-a-plugged-well) for examples.

sections.heading: Where does the data come from?
sections.body: From public databases, data files, and map services published by state oil and gas regulators and state geological surveys. For every record set, CAPIT shows the source agency, source system, retrieval date, verification date, and any known caveats.

sections.heading: Why doesn't CAPIT's count match a state's own report?
sections.body: States update on different schedules, CAPIT publishes a record only after it passes source checks, duplicates are removed, and some states report plugging paperwork processed rather than wells plugged. Each state page lists its coverage notes and latest refresh date.

sections.heading: Does each CAPIT token equal one well?
sections.body: One token is minted for each unique plugged-well record CAPIT publishes, so supply grows only as records are added. That is a rule about supply. It does not make a token a claim on a well, on any environmental benefit, or on anything else. The wells belong to their owners, the records belong to the public, and the token is separate from both.

sections.heading: What happens if a state corrects a record?
sections.body: CAPIT adds a new revision rather than overwriting the old one, so the full history stays visible and the record shows its current source status. The [Methodology](/methodology) explains how revisions are handled.

sections.heading: Is CAPIT a carbon credit?
sections.body: No. CAPIT does not measure or certify emissions reductions, and a CAPIT token cannot be used as a carbon credit or emissions offset. See [How Methane From Wells Is Measured](/how-methane-is-measured) for why we don't claim one.

sections.heading: Does CAPIT measure methane?
sections.body: No. CAPIT reports plugging records, not emissions. Most U.S. wells are never measured before or after plugging, and in July 2025 the federal orphan well program dropped its requirement that states measure. [How Methane From Wells Is Measured](/how-methane-is-measured) explains the methods, what changed, and why measurement matters.

sections.heading: Is the CAPIT token an investment?
sections.body: No, and please do not treat it as one. CAPIT is a community token with meme characteristics: its price depends on attention and demand, not on the registry or on wells being plugged. Tokens like this commonly lose most or all of their value. Never spend more than you can afford to lose. Nothing on this site is investment advice. Read the [Terms of Use](/terms-of-use) and the risks on the [Buy CAPIT](/buy-capit) page first.

sections.heading: What does holding CAPIT do?
sections.body: Today, nothing functional. The registry is free for everyone, with or without a token, and we intend to keep it that way. Proceeds from the token go toward the cost of building and running the registry, and we will publish how they are used. We would like holders to have recognition and a voice in decisions that do not affect the data itself. None of that exists yet, and we will say so here when it does.

sections.heading: Is CAPIT a meme token?
sections.body: Yes, in the sense that matters to anyone considering buying: its value comes from community and attention rather than from revenue or an underlying asset. We would rather say that plainly than dress it up. The registry and the token are separate things. The data is free to everyone, no wallet required, and holding CAPIT gives no claim on any well, any environmental benefit, or any public funds.

sections.heading: Is CAPIT affiliated with a government agency?
sections.body: No. CAPIT is independent. It uses records that state agencies publish, but it is not endorsed by or affiliated with any state agency or the U.S. Department of the Interior.

sections.heading: What network does CAPIT use?
sections.body: Base, an Ethereum layer-2 network. The [Buy CAPIT](/buy-capit) page lists the network, the full contract address, and a block-explorer link so you can confirm them before you connect a wallet.

sections.heading: Do I need a wallet to use the dashboard?
sections.body: No. Anyone can read, search, and compare records for free. You only need a wallet to buy or hold the token.

sections.heading: How do I report a data error?
sections.body: Use the [Contact](/contact) page and choose Data Correction. Include the state, the well's API number or source record ID, and a link to the source record if you have one.
